text.p: Italian bond futures hit new record highs on Wednesday with no sign that a market in thrall to rising expectations that Italy would make the first wave of EMU membership was about to come off the boil.
"The market is going like an express train," said a London-based futures trader. Data showing a surge in industrial orders in April added further fuel to a frenzied market.
Traders said that the September BTP LIFFE contract was now approaching a strong line of resistence at 137.00. "If it breaks through that level there will be a steep climb beyond," he said.
The spread between BTPs and the benchmark Bund also narrowed to a record 93 basis points.
Traders said the market appeared to be in no mood for a let-up now that fears of a possible delay to EMU's launch -- the worst possible scenario for Italy -- had receded well into the background.
"Everyone is jumping onto the bandwagon and we could see the spread go to 85 basis points in a very short space of time," said a futures trader. Andrew Hurst - Milan bureau +392-66102321
